result.title: A Tool in the Forward Pass: Frozen Tape Modules as Layers of a Small Language Model
result.comment: 12 pages, 1 figure, 9 tables. Code, configurations, results and frozen modules: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23831494
result.summary: Calling a tool through generated text adds decoding steps, even when the computation itself is short. We study an alternative: a small neural module that runs inside a language model's forward pass. A learned writer turns hidden states into a symbolic tape, a short sequence of discrete symbols that encodes the computation. The module, trained separately and then frozen, reduces the tape to a result, and a learned reader returns that result to the model. We evaluate arithmetic and object tracking in gemma-3-1b-it. With a writer trained on labelled tapes, the layer answers all 750 items of BIG-Bench Hard's tracking shuffled objects correctly. At seven people it needs about 1/10 of the GPU kernel time of a text-tool baseline that uses the same host model and exact code, with accuracy 1.00 against 0.99. The writer can also be learned from answers alone, guided by a hand-written copying prior, but less reliably: 5 of 6 runs succeed in the 1B host and 2 of 4 in the 4B host. Two independently trained layers keep their task accuracy when attached to one model, and a learned gate keeps them silent on the tested general-text and look-alike prompts. The results support a narrow use case: a bounded computation that returns one symbol can avoid the decoding cost of a textual tool call. Extracting the right input reliably, and deciding when to act, remain the main open problems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在小语言模型前向过程中嵌入独立训练后冻结的「磁带」模块：由 writer 将隐藏状态写成离散符号序列，模块计算后经 reader 把结果送回模型，并在算术和物体追踪任务上评估准确率、计算成本、多模块组合与门控行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其前向内部计算、离散状态接口、冻结模块组合及「何时发言」的门控，为 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被使用、贡献分配和停止/调用决策提供了可核查的方法线索；但工作纯文本且模块为符号计算，迁移到视觉推理仍需判断。
